identity.orderingGrade: The board declares DP83826AI or DP83826AE. Preserve that declaration separately from the two raw identity words. Both grades accept A114h in BASIC and A134h in ENHANCED with ID1 2000h. Require source review before admitting another revision.
identity.source: SNLS783A tables 8-22 and 8-23 specify ID1, the two mode-dependent models and revision 4. SNLS647I tables 8-21 and 8-22 give the same models at original revision 1. TI Linux A114/A134 use a revision-insensitive match. TI Linux NC A110 and Zephyr NC A131 disagree. SNLA491 table 2-4 prints A1x6 beside A111/A131 notes. None of those labels qualifies another revision or identifies a temperature grade.

sources.A: TI SNLS783A, October 2025, table 8-18 and sections 8.5.1.1 through 8.5.1.79
sources.original: TI SNLS647I, August 2025, table 8-17 and corresponding sections; dp83826i.json contains the original semantics and limits
sources.application: SNLS783A sections 8.3 and 8.4 include controls and procedures outside the summary table. Use the accompanying A procedure ledger for execution order, identity admission and procedure-specific exceptions.

interpretation.applicability: Every detailed row applies to each declared A suffix. The field and procedure conditions determine eligibility in BASIC and ENHANCED. The original comparison is with both I and E. Matching silicon observations cannot identify a temperature grade.
interpretation.comparison: originalField joins the id in dp83826i.json. Retain the referenced legal, prohibited, neutral, validity and readEffects semantics except where replaced in the A row. Use the A mask, access and reset for every operation. References in inherited text describe the original table. The A table at the enclosing record is the independent comparison source.
interpretation.access: Exact table 8-19 notation. Hardware H can change a bit without an application write. C reads consume evidence or mirror a latch with the field-specific clearing source. Command neutrality, W0C and explicit collector ownership take precedence over generic read-modify-write. A printed R/W on a reserved field grants no field-setting permission.
interpretation.reset: headerReset reproduces the register heading. Field reset strings are right-aligned, as printed. resetValue masked by resetKnownMask gives only board/mode-independent reset bits. Strap, OTP, mode variation and explicit X are excluded. Reset values for dynamic status describe the reset instant. They are unsuitable as live verification or write templates.
interpretation.reserved: reservedRows preserves the exact partitions, access and reset cells of the A table. Only an individually cited ordered procedure may use a reserved component of an exact recipe word.
interpretation.tests: For each named field, both declared grades require independent literal register/field masks and access checks, constrained reset comparisons, legal endpoint and prohibited-encoding cases where applicable. Every write starts with asymmetric neighboring bits and obeys field-specific neutral/consuming effects. Read-only fields and inaccessible routes must yield zero unauthorized writes. Read-to-clear and cross-register mirror tests retain the first observation after partial failure.
interpretation.aliases: SNLS783A 8.3.11.1 exposes the direct low standard registers via vendor MMD. REGCR and ADDAR are selector primitives and have no ordinary payload aliases. The printed IEEE EEE namespaces use their explicitly selected tuples.
